{{Quote|We conquered whole star systems. We had an empire. When cities heard our armies were coming, populations fled before a shot was fired. Now we cling to a pathetic sector of dirtball planets, we scramble for the crumbs that the cowardly ''aruetiise'' throw when they want us to fight for them, and they use us as a breeding stock for their clone armies. The ''aruetiise'' will always treat us like an animal species to be used for their convenience until we stand up for ourselves again.|Lorka Gedyc|<ref name="ImpCom501st" />}}
'''Lorka Gedyc''' was a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] of [[Clan Gedyc]], and a member of the radical Mandalorian splinter group known as the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]. By the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Declaration of a New Order|foundation]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Gedyc had become the organization's most recent [[Secret Mandalore|leader]] as it continued to exist in hiding, moving to ally Death Watch with the Empire.

==Biography==
Following the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Gedyc had become the [[Secret Mandalore|leader]] of the [[Death/Legends|Death]] Watch. Gedyc thought highly of the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorians]] of ages past, who had [[Mandalorian Wars|conquered]] [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and forged an empire<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> that spanned across vast swaths of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The state of the greatly diminished [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] following the defeat of [[Mandalore the Ultimate]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> was abhorrent to Gedyc, who considered Mandalorian holdings in [[Republic Classic era|the era]] to be little more than an assortment of "dirtball" [[Planet/Legends|worlds]], and felt that the Mandalorians' penchant for [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]] work was tantamount to scrambling for crumbs.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

Seeing this as an opportunity to restore the glory the Death Watch leader believed the Mandalorians had lost, Gedyc allied Death Watch with the Galactic Empire, and the Death Watch soldiers [[Dred Priest]] and [[Isabet Reau]] assisted the Imperials in establishing their [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]]<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> on the Mandalorian [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]],<ref name="TEA" /> just outside the planetary [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], in the failed adventure park<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> known as the "[[City of Bone]]."<ref name="TEA" /> Priest thought highly of Gedyc and the Death Watch leader's plans, and like Gedyc, saw the Empire as an opportunity to re-establish the Mandalorians' former power.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Lorka Gedyc has big plans for us.|[[Dred Priest]], discussing Lorka Gedyc in the novel ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''|<ref name="ImpCom501st" />}}
Lorka Gedyc was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[2009]] novel ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]'', the fifth entry in [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]]' [[Republic Commando|''Republic'' and ''Imperial Commando'' series]].
